entry: Malaysian politician and physician, prime minister in 1981–2003 and again in 2018–2020. Born in Alor Setar, he entered parliament in 1964 and became deputy prime minister in 1976. His first tenure brought rapid industrialization, privatization and major infrastructure projects, including the North–South Expressway and the Kuala Lumpur City Centre, and Malaysia recovered relatively quickly from the 1997 Asian financial crisis, aided by capital controls. He supported an amendment that removed royal criminal immunity, a move widely regarded as strengthening the [[Rule of law|rule of law]]. Critics accused him of [[Authoritarianism|authoritarianism]] for centralizing power and suppressing dissent, while supporters argued his actions preserved national stability. In 1998 the dismissal of his deputy, Anwar Ibrahim, sparked the *Reformasi* movement. He resigned in 2003, but in 2018 he led the Pakatan Harapan coalition to victory, secured Anwar's pardon and served until resigning in 2020.

Indian religious reformer, considered by [[Jainism|Jains]] to be the 24th and final *Tirthankara* of the current time cycle. According to tradition, he was born into a royal family in what is now [[Bihar]], India, and renounced his worldly possessions at about 30 to become an [[Asceticism|ascetic]]. After years of meditation and austerity he attained *kevala jnana* (omniscience) and preached for 30 years. His teachings stress the five vows of *ahimsa* (non-violence), *satya* (truthfulness), *asteya* (non-stealing), *brahmacharya* (chastity) and *aparigraha* (non-attachment), and the many-sided nature of reality known as *anekantavada*. Historians regard his existence as well established, though the dates of his life are uncertain. His teachings were compiled as the Jain Agamas. Jains observe his [[Nirvana|nirvana]] at [[Diwali]].

American actor and two-time [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] winner. He won Best Supporting Actor for *Moonlight* (2016) and *Green Book* (2018), becoming the first Black actor to win two Academy Awards in the same category. He gained wider attention through [[House of Cards (American TV series)|House of Cards]] and later played a troubled police officer in the third season of the [[HBO]] series *True Detective*. He also voiced Aaron Davis in *Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse*. The family of Don Shirley disputed the film's portrayal of his relationship with his driver. Ali later apologized to the family but maintained the film's emotional authenticity.

Surface-dwelling ray-finned fish, also called common dolphinfish or dorado, found in offshore temperate, tropical and subtropical waters worldwide. It is most common around the [[Gulf of Mexico]], [[Costa Rica]], [[Hawaii]] and the [[Indian Ocean]]. The name comes from Hawaiian and means very strong, and despite its alternate name, the fish is not related to [[Dolphin|dolphins]]. Males develop a prominent forehead hump as they mature. The fish has dazzling colors, golden on the sides and blue or green on the back, which fade to muted yellow-grey after death. Catches typically weigh 7 to 13 kg, and the fish can live up to five years. Females may spawn two or three times a year, producing 80,000 to 1,000,000 eggs per event. It feeds on [[Flying fish|flying fish]], [[Squid|squid]] and crustaceans, and can swim as fast as 50 knots.

Tile-based game of Chinese origin for two to four players, played with a set of 144 tiles based on [[Chinese characters]] and symbols. Players draw and discard tiles to form four melds (sets) and a pair, and may also win with special hands. Rules and scoring vary by region, and the game mixes skill, strategy and luck, much like the Western [[Card game|card game]] rummy. Developed in China in the 19th century, it spread internationally from the early 20th century and has been adapted into widely played online entertainment. Its origin is disputed, with [[Ningbo]] and [[Fujian]] both proposed. The name means sparrow in several southern Chinese languages, a reference to the clacking sound of shuffled tiles.

Ottoman sultan (r. 1808–1839), often described as the "Peter the Great of Turkey". He came to power after an 1808 coup in which his half-brother Mustafa IV was deposed and his cousin, [[Selim III]], was killed. In the 1826 Auspicious Incident he disbanded the conservative [[Janissary|Janissary corps]], removing a major obstacle to reform and paving the way for a modern army. He recentralized the [[Ottoman Empire]], restructured its bureaucracy and established a Council of Ministers. The empire lost Bessarabia to Russia early in his reign and Algeria to France from 1830, and he was forced to recognize the independent Greek state in 1832 after the [[Greek War of Independence]]. He died of [[Tuberculosis|tuberculosis]] and was succeeded by his son Abdülmecid I, who continued his modernization efforts.

Ghaznavid sultan (r. 998–1030) who extended a military empire from northwestern Iran to the [[Punjab]]. Born in Ghazni, in present-day [[Afghanistan]], he was the first ruler to hold the title sultan. A champion of [[Sunni Islam]], he waged war on non-Muslim states in the Indian subcontinent and on Shi'a states within and beyond his empire. He made 35 major and 11 minor campaigns in a 32-year reign and conquered [[Lahore]], laying foundations for Muslim rule in the Punjab. He is reputed to have been undefeated throughout his military career. His capital, Ghazni, became a major cultural and intellectual center, attracting scholars such as [[Al-Biruni|al-Biruni]] and the poet [[Ferdowsi|Ferdowsi]]. He also patronized Persian literature and Islamic scholarship.

Reddish-brown timber from three tropical hardwood species of the genus *Swietenia*, native to the [[Americas]]. It is valued for its color, durability and workability, and is used for furniture, [[Cabinetry|cabinetry]], boats and musical instruments. *Swietenia macrophylla*, Honduran or big-leaf mahogany, is the most widespread species and the only one widely grown commercially. European use began in the late 16th century, and trade expanded after the mid-17th century, especially under British colonial rule in the [[Caribbean]]. By the 18th and 19th centuries mahogany was a major global commodity. Overexploitation led to the 2003 listing of *S. macrophylla* on CITES Appendix II, the first high-volume tropical timber species to receive that level of protection. In some regions, notably the [[Philippines]], mahogany is considered environmentally problematic.

City (pop., 2022: c. 2,000,000, metropolitan area), capital and largest city of Borno State in northeastern [[Nigeria]]. It lies along the seasonal Ngadda River, which disappears into swamps near [[Lake Chad]], and was long part of the [[Kanem–Bornu Empire]]. The British founded it in 1907 as a military outpost and chose it as their military headquarters in 1908. The railway reached the city in 1964, spurring its growth as a commercial center. Boko Haram was founded in Maiduguri in 2002 by cleric Mohammed Yusuf, and the city is the group's most frequent target. In late July 2009 Boko Haram violence left over 700 people dead, and in March 2015 five suicide bombings killed 54.

Chemical reaction between [[Amino acid|amino acids]] and reducing sugars, responsible for the browning and flavor of cooked food. It typically proceeds rapidly from around 140 to 165 °C (280 to 330 °F). Its products include melanoidins, which brown food, and hundreds of flavor compounds that give seared meat, [[Bread|bread]] and coffee their character. It is named after French chemist Louis Camille Maillard, who first described it in 1912. Nobel laureate Jean-Marie Lehn called it "the most widely practiced chemical reaction in the world." At high temperatures it can form acrylamide, a probable [[Carcinogen|carcinogen]].

Sephardic Jewish [[Rabbi|rabbi]], philosopher and physician, also called Rambam. Born in Córdoba, he was exiled from Muslim-ruled Spain after the Almohads took Córdoba in 1148. He lived in Fez, Acre, Jerusalem and Alexandria before settling in Fustat, Egypt, where he became personal physician to [[Saladin]]. Jews as far away as Iraq and Yemen acclaimed his writings on halakha and Jewish ethics, and he led the Jewish community in Egypt. His fourteen-volume *Mishneh Torah* codifies [[Halakha|halakha]] and still carries significant authority in [[Judaism]], as do his thirteen principles of faith. Influenced by [[Aristotle]] and [[Al-Farabi|al-Farabi]], he also contributed to Islamic science and philosophy. He is said to be buried in [[Tiberias]], a site of Jewish pilgrimage.

Continuous band of stars on a [[Hertzsprung–Russell diagram|Hertzsprung–Russell diagram]] of stellar color against brightness, where stars spend most of their lives. During this phase core hydrogen fusion into helium dominates. The heat produced creates a pressure gradient that balances gravitational collapse, keeping the star in [[Hydrostatic equilibrium|hydrostatic equilibrium]]. Main-sequence stars, also called dwarf stars, are the most numerous true stars in the universe and include the [[Sun]]. A star's position on the band depends mainly on its mass. Stars below about 1.5 solar masses fuse hydrogen mainly through the proton–proton chain, while more massive stars use the CNO cycle, in which carbon, nitrogen and oxygen act as intermediaries. More massive stars leave the main sequence sooner, evolving into [[Red giant|red giants]] or [[Supergiant|supergiants]] once hydrogen is exhausted.

State in the [[New England]] region of the northeastern [[United States]]. Its capital is Augusta and its largest city is Portland. Known as the Pine Tree State, it is the most rural U.S. state, with a rocky [[Atlantic Ocean|Atlantic]] coastline, forested interior, and wild lowbush blueberries and lobster. Indigenous Wabanaki peoples inhabited the territory for about 12,000 years before European arrival. Maine was part of [[Massachusetts]] until 1820, when it was admitted to the Union as the 23rd state under the Missouri Compromise. Its population was an estimated 1,400,000 in 2024, its highest-ever estimate.

Large domesticated [[Cat|cat]] breed that originated in [[Maine]], where it is the official state cat. It is selectively bred from one of the oldest landraces in North America, and its long, dense coat and large tufted paws help it survive harsh winters. Myths claim it is a hybrid with a [[Raccoon|raccoon]] or [[Bobcat|bobcat]], but genetic studies show its closest European relatives are cats found in the [[United Kingdom]]. Popular at late 19th-century cat shows, its existence was threatened after long-haired breeds were imported in the early 20th century. It has since recovered and is the most popular breed in several global registries.

Continental portion of [[Southeast Asia]], historically known as Indochina. It comprises Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Peninsular Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, and borders [[East Asia]] to the north and [[South Asia]] to the west. The term Indochina was coined in the early 19th century and was later adopted for the French colony of [[French Indochina]], covering present-day Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam. After the [[Vietnam War]], the term fell out of use in favor of Mainland Southeast Asia. Mountain ranges extend from the Tibetan Plateau, and the lowlands are largely drained by three major river systems, including the [[Mekong]]. Much of the mainland historically practiced [[Theravada]] Buddhism, while the east coast was home to the Confucian kingdom of Đại Việt.

[[Java|Javanese]] Hindu-Buddhist *thalassocratic* empire, 1292–1527. Founded by Raden Wijaya after a Mongol invasion of Java, it reached its peak under Queen Tribhuvana and her son Hayam Wuruk in the mid-14th century, with prime minister [[Gajah Mada]] credited for many conquests. The *Nagarakṛtāgama* of 1365 describes 98 tributaries stretching from [[Sumatra]] to [[New Guinea]], although historians debate the scope of its influence. After a civil war weakened control over its vassal states, the empire declined and fell in 1527 to an invasion by the Sultanate of Demak, after which Islamic kingdoms rose in Java. It is sometimes seen as a precedent for the modern boundaries of [[Indonesia]].

Professional [[Baseball|baseball]] league of 30 teams, 29 in the United States and one in [[Canada]], divided into the National and American leagues. It is headquartered in [[New York City]]. Each team plays 162 games per season, and the champion is decided in the [[World Series]], a best-of-seven series first played in 1903. The two leagues agreed in the National Agreement of 1903 to respect each other's contracts, but remained legally separate until 2000. After the Black Sox Scandal of 1919, the commissioner was given near-unlimited authority over the sport. Shortly after [[World War II]], [[Jackie Robinson|Jackie Robinson]] broke baseball's color barrier. In 2025 MLB drew 71.4 million spectators, the highest total season attendance of any sports league in the world. The [[New York Yankees]] have won the most World Series championships, with 27.

Professional soccer league in North America and the top level of the U.S. soccer league system. It has 30 teams, 27 in the United States and 3 in Canada, and is headquartered in [[New York City]]. Founded in 1993 as part of the United States' successful bid to host the [[FIFA World Cup|1994 FIFA World Cup]], it began play in 1996 with ten teams. Its predecessor, the North American Soccer League, operated from 1968 to 1984. Each team is owned by the league, and it is one of few major soccer leagues without promotion and relegation. The LA Galaxy have won the most MLS Cups, with six.

[[Mood disorder|Mood disorder]], also called [[Depression (mood)|clinical depression]], marked by at least two weeks of pervasive low mood, low self-esteem and loss of interest in normally enjoyable activities. Diagnosis rests on clinical evaluation, including reports from family or friends and a mental status examination, because no laboratory test exists for it. About 40% of the risk is genetic, and risk factors include family history, major life changes, childhood trauma and substance use disorders. It causes the second-most years lived with disability, after lower back pain. Symptoms can include hopelessness, emotional blunting, poor concentration, insomnia or hypersomnia, and changes in appetite. Treatment usually combines [[Psychotherapy|psychotherapy]] with antidepressant [[Medication|medication]], such as [[Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor|SSRIs]], although the clinical efficacy of antidepressants is disputed. Untreated, it increases the risk of [[Suicide|suicide]], the 11th leading cause of death in the U.S.

City (pop., mid-2025: 1,485,000), capital of South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Located on the southwest coast of [[Sulawesi]], facing the Makassar Strait, it is the largest city in eastern Indonesia. An important trading port, it hosted the center of the Gowa Sultanate and a Portuguese naval base before the [[Dutch East India Company]] conquered it in the 17th century. It remained a major port in the [[Dutch East Indies]]. In 1950 the Makassar Uprising led to integration into the Republic of Indonesia. The city was renamed Ujung Pandang from 1971 to 1999 before reverting to Makassar under President B. J. Habibie. Its metropolitan area, Mamminasata, had a population of about 2,795,639 in mid-2025.

Dwarf planet in the [[Kuiper belt]], the fourth-largest dwarf planet and trans-Neptunian object in the [[Solar System]]. Michael E. Brown, Chad Trujillo and David Rabinowitz discovered it in 2005 at Palomar Observatory, and their discovery contributed to [[Pluto|Pluto]]'s reclassification as a dwarf planet. Its diameter is 60% that of Pluto, and its reddish-brown surface is covered largely by frozen methane. Gaseous methane has been detected around it, and it may harbor a subsurface ocean of liquid water. No space probe has visited it, so no close-up images of its surface exist.

Malay sultanate based in present-day Malacca, Malaysia. Conventionally dated to c. 1400, it was founded by Parameswara, also known as Iskandar Shah. At its height in the 15th century, its capital was one of the most important transshipment ports of its time, with territory covering much of the [[Malay Peninsula]], the Riau Islands and part of eastern [[Sumatra]]. It became a center of Islamic learning, and [[Malay language|Classical Malay]] became the [[Lingua franca|lingua franca]] of Maritime Southeast Asia. In 1511 the [[Portuguese Empire]] captured the capital, and the last sultan, Mahmud Shah, retreated south, where his descendants founded the Johor and Perak dynasties. The concept of *daulat*, a distinctly Malay notion of sovereignty, continues to shape ideas of Malay kingship.

Opaque, green-banded copper carbonate hydroxide [[Mineral|mineral]], Cu₂(CO₃)(OH)₂. It forms in weathered copper ore deposits, often with azurite, and usually as botryoidal, fibrous or stalactitic masses in fractures and underground spaces. Its name derives from the Greek for mallow-green stone, reflecting its resemblance to mallow leaves, and [[Copper|copper]] gives it its green color. It has been used as an ornamental stone and gemstone for millennia, and [[Ancient Egypt|Ancient Egyptians]] ground it into a green pigment. It has been mined and smelted for copper at Timna Valley in [[Israel]] for more than 3,000 years.

Largest class of crustaceans, with about 40,000 living species in 16 orders. Members include crabs, lobsters, crayfish, shrimp, [[Krill|krill]], isopods and [[Mantis shrimp|mantis shrimp]], and they inhabit marine, freshwater and terrestrial environments. Their bodies have 20 segments (rarely 21), divided into a head, thorax and abdomen. Except for fairy shrimps, malacostracans are the only living arthropods with compound eyes on movable stalks. [[Decapod|Decapods]], such as shrimp and crabs, support major fisheries, and krill form a foundation of marine food webs. The name, from the Greek for soft shell, is a misnomer because the shell is usually hard. French zoologist Pierre André Latreille applied it in 1802.

[[Austronesian languages|Austronesian]] language and dialect continuum spoken in [[Madagascar]], alongside French as an official language. Spoken by about 25 million people in Madagascar and the [[Comoros]], it is the westernmost Austronesian language, brought to the island by settlers from the Sunda Islands. It is most closely related to Maʼanyan, spoken in [[Borneo]]. After c. 1000 AD it absorbed numerous [[Bantu languages|Bantu]] and Arabic loanwords. It has about a dozen dialects in three main groups, and the Merina dialect of the central plateau is the basis of Standard Malagasy, used by government and media. It is written in the [[Latin script]], introduced by Western missionaries in the early 19th century, replacing the earlier Sorabe script, a local form of the Arabic script.
